You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# thokr
✨ sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

[![GitHub Build Workflow](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/actions/workflows/build.yml)

[![Crate Version](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/thokr)](https://crates.io/crates/thokr)
[![Github Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/thatvegandev/thokr)](https://github.com/thatvegandev/thokr/stargazers)

![demo](https://github.com/thatvegandev/assets/raw/main/thokr/demo.gif)

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

```
thokr 0.4.1
sleek typing tui with visualized results and historical logging

USAGE:
    thokr [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS:
    -f, --full-sentences <NUMBER_OF_SENTENCES>
            number of sentences to use in test

    -h, --help
            Print help information

    -l, --supported-language <SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE>
            language to pull words from [default: english] [possible values: english, english1k,
            english10k]

    -p, --prompt <PROMPT>
            custom prompt to use

    -s, --number-of-secs <NUMBER_OF_SECS>
            number of seconds to run test

    -V, --version
            Print version information

    -w, --number-of-words <NUMBER_OF_WORDS>
            number of words to use in test [default: 15]

```


## Installation

### Cargo

```sh
$ cargo install thokr
```

### Docker

```sh
$ docker run -it thatvegandev/thokr
```

### Arch Linux

Install `thokr-git` from the AUR

## Usage

For detailed usage run `thokr -h`.

### Examples

| command                     |                                                    test contents |
|:----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------:|
| `thokr`                     |                          50 of the 200 most common english words |
| `thokr -w 100`              |                         100 of the 200 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 100 -l english1k` |                        100 of the 1000 most common English words |
| `thokr -w 10 -s 5`          | 10 of the 200 most common English words (hard stop at 5 seconds) |
| `thokr -p "$(cat foo.txt)"` |                   custom prompt with the output of `cat foo.txt` |
| `thokr -f 4`                | 4 grammatical sentences with full stops; overrides word settings |

_During a test you can press ← to start over or → to see a new prompt (assuming
you didn't supply a custom one)_

## Supported Languages

The following languages are available by default:

| name         |                     description |
| :----------- | ------------------------------: |
| `english`    |   200 most common English words |
| `english1k`  |  1000 most common English words |
| `english10k` | 10000 most common English words |

## Logging

Upon completion of a test, a row outlining your results is appended to the
`log.csv` file found in the following platform-specific folders. This way you
can easily track your progress over time.

| platform | value                                                            |                                        example |
| :------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------: |
| Linux    | $XDG*CONFIG_HOME/\_project_path* or $HOME/.config/_project_path_ |                      /home/colby/.config/thokr |
| macOS    | $HOME/Library/Application Support/_project_path_                 | /Users/Colby/Library/Application Support/thokr |
| Windows  | {FOLDERID*RoamingAppData}\_project_path*\config                  |    C:\Users\Colby\AppData\Roaming\thokr\config |

{"command":"cat <<'PY' > /tmp/cap.py
import pty, os, sys, time, select
cmd = sys.argv[1:]
pid, fd = pty.fork()
if pid==0:
    os.environ["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
    os.execv(cmd[0], cmd)
else:
    # set winsize
    import fcntl, termios, struct
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", 24, 80, 0,0))
    out=b""
    time.sleep(1.0)
    while True:
        r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.2)
        if not r: break
        try: d=os.read(fd, 65536)
        except: break
        if not d: break
        out+=d
    sys.stdout.buffer.write(out)
    # try quit with ctrl-c?
    try:
        os.write(fd, b'\x03')
    except: pass
    time.sleep(0.5)
    while True:
        r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.2)
        if not r: break
        try: d=os.read(fd, 65536)
        except: break
        if not d: break
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(d)
PY
python3 /tmp/cap.py ./executable -p "hello world" > /tmp/out1.bin 2>&1; echo exit:$?; wc -c /tmp/out1.bin; cat -v /tmp/out1.bin | head -c 8000; echo
"}

import pty, os, sys, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct, shutil, subprocess, signal

def run_session(args, actions, rows=24, cols=80, home="/tmp/fakehome"):
    # actions: list of (delay_before, bytes or None)
    shutil.rmtree(home, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(home+"/.config", exist_ok=True)
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid==0:
        os.environ["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
        os.environ["HOME"]=home
        # XDG maybe unset?
        os.environ.pop("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", None)
        os.execv(args[0], args)
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", rows, cols, 0,0))
    out=b""
    def drain(timeout=0.3):
        nonlocal out
        end=time.time()+timeout
        chunk=b""
        while time.time()<end:
            r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[], max(0,end-time.time()))
            if not r: break
            try: d=os.read(fd, 65536)
            except: break
            if not d: break
            chunk+=d; out+=d
            end=time.time()+0.05  # extend a bit?
        return chunk
    drain(0.6)
    snapshots=[]
    for delay,data in actions:
        if delay: 
            c=drain(delay)
            snapshots.append((f"wait{delay}",c))
        if data:
            os.write(fd, data)
            c=drain(0.4)
            snapshots.append((f"sent{data!r}",c))
    # try esc exit
    try: os.write(fd, b'\x1b')
    except: pass
    drain(0.4)
    try:
        pid2,status=os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
        if pid2==0:
            os.kill(pid, signal.SIGKILL); os.waitpid(pid,0)
    except: pass
    logpath=home+"/.config/thokr/log.csv"
    log=open(logpath).read() if os.path.exists(logpath) else None
    return out, snapshots, log

if __name__=="__main__":

    print("LOG",log)
    print("SNAPS",[(k,len(v)) for k,v in snaps])
    print(out[-500:])

import pty, os, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct, shutil
shutil.rmtree("/tmp/fhtiming",ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs("/tmp/fhtiming",exist_ok=True)
pid, fd = pty.fork()
if pid==0:
    os.environ["TERM"]="xterm-256color"; os.environ["HOME"]="/tmp/fhtiming"; os.environ.pop("XDG_CONFIG_HOME",None)
    os.execv("./executable",["./executable","-p","abcdefghij"])
fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH",24,80,0,0))
time.sleep(0.5)
# drain
while select.select([fd],[],[],0)[0]:
    os.read(fd,65536)
t0=time.time(); os.write(fd,b"abcdefghij")
while time.time()-t0<2:
    r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.5)
    if r:
        d=os.read(fd,65536)
        print(f"{time.time()-t0:.4f} len={len(d)} {d[:80]!r}")
    # check done?
print("done")
try: os.kill(pid,9)
except: pass

import pty, os, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct, shutil
def run(prompt, first, rest, wait, home):
    shutil.rmtree(home, ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(home, exist_ok=True)
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid==0:
        os.environ["TERM"]="xterm-256color"; os.environ["HOME"]=home; os.environ.pop("XDG_CONFIG_HOME",None)
        os.execv("./executable",["./executable","-p",prompt])
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH",24,80,0,0))
    # read initial
    data=b""
    while b'?25l' not in data:
        r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],1)
        if r: data+=os.read(fd,65536)
    os.write(fd, first.encode())
    # read char draw
    data=b""
    while b'?25l' not in data:
        r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],1)
        if r: data+=os.read(fd,65536)
    t_first_draw=time.time()
    time.sleep(wait)
    os.write(fd, rest.encode())
    time.sleep(0.05)
    # wait for log
    logp=home+"/.config/thokr/log.csv"
    for _ in range(100):
        if os.path.exists(logp): break
        time.sleep(0.01)
    log=open(logp).read().splitlines()[-1] if os.path.exists(logp) else None
    try: os.write(fd,b'\x1b')
    except: pass
    time.sleep(0.05)
    try: os.kill(pid,9); os.waitpid(pid,0)
    except: pass
    return log

for wait in [0.05,0.15,0.25,0.35,0.55,0.95,1.05,1.95]:
    print("wait",wait, run("abcdefghij","a","bcdefghij",wait,f"/tmp/fhprec{int(wait*100)}"))

import pty, os, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct, shutil

def run(prompt, schedule, home, extra_args=[]):
    shutil.rmtree(home, ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(home, exist_ok=True)
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid==0:
        os.environ["TERM"]="xterm-256color"; os.environ["HOME"]=home; os.environ.pop("XDG_CONFIG_HOME",None)
        os.execv("./executable",["./executable"]+extra_args+["-p",prompt])
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH",24,80,0,0))
    data=b""
    while b'?25l' not in data:
        r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],1)
        if r: data+=os.read(fd,65536)
    t0=time.time()
    for t,s in schedule:
        now=time.time()-t0
        if t>now: time.sleep(t-now)
        if s: os.write(fd, s.encode())
    # wait log
    logp=home+"/.config/thokr/log.csv"; log=None
    for _ in range(200):
        if os.path.exists(logp):
            log=open(logp).read().splitlines()[-1]; break
        time.sleep(0.01)
    try: os.write(fd,b'\x1b')
    except: pass
    time.sleep(0.02)
    try: os.kill(pid,9); os.waitpid(pid,0)
    except: pass
    return log

def trial(label, prompt, schedule, extra=[]):
    log=run(prompt, schedule, f"/tmp/fhsch{abs(hash(label))%99999}", extra)
    print(label, "->", log)

def jaro(s1,s2):
    if s1==s2: return 1.0
    l1,l2=len(s1),len(s2)
    if not l1 or not l2: return 0.0
    match_dist=max(l1,l2)//2-1
    m1=[False]*l1; m2=[False]*l2; matches=0
    for i,ch in enumerate(s1):
        lo=max(0,i-match_dist); hi=min(l2,i+match_dist+1)
        for j in range(lo,hi):
            if not m2[j] and s2[j]==ch:
                m1[i]=True; m2[j]=True; matches+=1; break
    if matches==0: return 0.0
    t=0; k=0
    for i in range(l1):
        if m1[i]:
            while not m2[k]: k+=1
            if s1[i]!=s2[k]: t+=1
            k+=1
    t//=2
    return (matches/l1+matches/l2+(matches-t)/matches)/3

for inp in ["number-of-wordsx","number-of-word","number-o-words","numbe-of-words","number-of-wor","number-of"]:
    print(inp, "words jaro",jaro(inp,"number-of-words"), "secs jaro",jaro(inp,"number-of-secs"))

import pty, os, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct, shutil, sys
def run(seq, label, prompt="hello"):
    home=f"/tmp/fhkey{abs(hash(label))%99999}"
    shutil.rmtree(home,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(home,exist_ok=True)
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid==0:
        fcntl.ioctl(1, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH",24,80,0,0))
        os.environ["TERM"]="xterm-256color"; os.environ["HOME"]=home; os.environ.pop("XDG_CONFIG_HOME",None)
        os.execv("./executable",["./executable","-p",prompt])
    def drain(t=0.35):
        data=b""; end=time.time()+t
        while time.time()<end:
            r,_,_=select.select([fd],[],[],0.03)
            if r:
                try: d=os.read(fd,65536)
                except: break
                data+=d
        return data
    drain()
    alive_before=True
    os.write(fd, seq)
    out=drain(0.4)
    # check alive
    p,status=os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
    alive=(p==0)
    screen_hint=out[-200:]
    if alive:
        try: os.write(fd,b'\x1b'); drain(0.2); os.kill(pid,9); os.waitpid(pid,0)
        except: pass
    logp=home+"/.config/thokr/log.csv"
    log=open(logp).read() if os.path.exists(logp) else None
    print(f"{label} seq={seq!r} alive={alive} log={bool(log)} out_tail={screen_hint!r}")

import pty,os,time,select,fcntl,termios,struct
pid,fd=pty.fork()

    os.environ["TERM"]="xterm-256color"
    os.execv("./executable",["./executable","-p","hi"])

time.sleep(0.4)
while select.select([fd],[],[],0)[0]: data+=os.read(fd,65536)

while select.select([fd],[],[],0)[0]: data+=os.read(fd,65536)
print("results tail",data[-200:])

print("after r",data)
os.write(fd,b'\x1b'); time.sleep(0.4); data=b""
while select.select([fd],[],[],0)[0]: data+=os.read(fd,65536)
print("exit bytes",data)
print("wait",os.waitpid(pid,0))

def pop(v):
    m=sum(v)/len(v); return math.sqrt(sum((x-m)**2 for x in v)/len(v))
def samp(v):
    m=sum(v)/len(v); return math.sqrt(sum((x-m)**2 for x in v)/(len(v)-1)) if len(v)>1 else 0
def make(B,s,var):
    if var=="base": return [B]+[1]*s
    if var=="plus0": return [B]+[1]*s+[0]
    if var=="pre0": return [0,B]+[1]*s
    if var=="plus0pre0": return [0,B]+[1]*s+[0]
    if var=="firstplus1": return [B+1]+[1]*(s-1) if s>=1 else [B]
    if var=="firstplus1_plus0": return [B+1]+[1]*(s-1)+[0]
    if var=="Bminus1_first": return [B-1,1]+[1]*s  # split burst across?
    if var=="counts_plus_final1": return [B]+[1]*s+[1]

# recompute pop tick
def pop_tick(B,s):
    vals=[]
    for k in range(1,s*10+1):
        t=k/10; stage=0 if t<1 else min(int(math.floor(t)),s)
        v=B*12 if stage==0 else (B+stage)*12/(stage+1)
        vals.append(v)
    m=sum(vals)/len(vals); return math.sqrt(sum((x-m)**2 for x in vals)/len(vals))

for (B,s),o in obs.items():

import sys, math
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from sched import run
def predict(prompt, schedule):
    # schedule entries absolute times; chars correct if matches prompt at sequential position
    counts={}
    pos=0; final_sec=None
    events=[]
    for t,s in schedule:
        for ch in s:
            correct = pos < len(prompt) and ch==prompt[pos]
            events.append((t,pos,ch,correct)); pos+=1
    if events:
        final_sec=math.floor(events[-1][0]+1e-9)  # approx; driver adds tiny overhead
    for t,p,ch,correct in events:
        sec=math.floor(t+1e-9)
        if correct and sec!=final_sec:
            counts[sec]=counts.get(sec,0)+1
    vals=list(counts.values())
    if not vals: return 0.0, vals
    m=sum(vals)/len(vals); return math.sqrt(sum((x-m)**2 for x in vals)/len(vals)), vals

tests=[
 ("abcdefghij",[(0,"abcde"),(1.3,"f"),(2.7,"g"),(3.2,"hij")]),
 ("abcdefghij",[(0,"ab"),(0.4,"cd"),(1.9,"ef"),(2.1,"g"),(4.8,"hij")]),
 ("abcdefghijklmnop",[(0,"abcde"),(1.2,"fgh"),(2.9,"ijk"),(3.5,"lm"),(5.5,"nop")]),
 ("abcdefghij",[(0,"xbcde"),(1.2,"f"),(2.2,"ghij")]), # first char wrong
 ("abcdefghij",[(0,"abc"),(3.7,"defg"),(4.2,"hij")]),
]
for prompt,sched in tests:
    log=run(prompt,sched,f"/tmp/fhpred{abs(hash(str(sched)))%9999}")
    pred,vals=predict(prompt,sched)
    print(f"sched={sched} vals={vals} pred_sd={pred:.2f} log={log}")
PY"}

import subprocess,time,os,shutil
def get(binpath):
    home="/tmp/cmp_home"; shutil.rmtree(home,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(home)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"],stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL); time.sleep(0.08)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","new-session","-d","-s","t","-x","80","-y","24",f'HOME={home} {binpath} -p "abcdefghij"']); time.sleep(0.45)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","t","-l","a"]); time.sleep(1.0)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","t","-l","bcdefghij"]); time.sleep(0.3)
    r=subprocess.run(["tmux","capture-pane","-t","t","-p"],capture_output=True,text=True)
    subprocess.run(["tmux","kill-server"],stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    for row,l in enumerate(r.stdout.splitlines()):
        for col,ch in enumerate(l):
            if '\u2800' <= ch <= '\u28ff':
                bits=ord(ch)-0x2800; ds=[]
                for dc,dr,bit in [(0,0,1),(0,1,2),(0,2,4),(1,0,8),(1,1,16),(1,2,32),(0,3,64),(1,3,128)]:
                    if bits&bit: ds.append((dc,dr))
                print(binpath, f"cell({col},{row}) dots{ds}")
    print()
get("./executable")
get("./target/release/executable")

lines=[]
lines.append("//! Rendering helpers for the typing prompt.")
lines.append("")
lines.append("//! The prompt widget conceptually separates three regions of the")
lines.append("//! prompt string while it draws a frame:")
lines.append("//!")
lines.append("//! * the prefix that has already been typed, coloured by correctness;")
lines.append("//! * the single current character, emphasised with an underline; and")
lines.append("//! * the remaining suffix, shown dimmed until it is reached.")
lines.append("//!")
lines.append("//! Those regions are obtained by slicing the prompt string. The")
lines.append("//! slice offsets are the caller's character positions used directly")
lines.append("//! as byte offsets into the string. For plain ASCII prompts, which")
lines.append("//! cover generated tests and the overwhelming majority of custom")
lines.append("//! prompts, character positions and byte offsets coincide and")
lines.append("//! the regions line up exactly with the visible text.")
lines.append("//!")
lines.append("//! Multi-byte characters are the awkward corner. A character with")
lines.append("//! a multi-byte encoding occupies several bytes, so using the")
lines.append("//! character position as a byte offset lands in the middle of")
lines.append("//! that character instead of on a boundary. Rust strings reject")
lines.append("//! slices that do not start and end on character boundaries.")
lines.append("//!")
lines.append("//! The helper in this module intentionally keeps that behaviour.")
lines.append("//! It takes the prompt and the position of the current character")
lines.append("//! and slices out the one-byte-wide current region. Rendering a")
lines.append("//! prompt whose current character is multi-byte therefore")
lines.append("//! fails in exactly the same way as the reference program.")
lines.append("//!")
lines.append("//! Keeping the slice in its own tiny function also keeps the")
lines.append("//! slicing policy in one place: callers pass the whole prompt")
lines.append("//! and a character position, and this module owns the indexing.")
lines.append("//!")
lines.append("//! The rest of the drawing code works with owned characters and")
lines.append("//! display widths, so it never has to reason about byte offsets.")
lines.append("//!")
lines.append("//! Note that the panic, when it happens, is raised while a frame")
lines.append("//! is being drawn, before any part of that frame is flushed to")
lines.append("//! the terminal. The alternate screen has already been entered")
lines.append("//! at that point, so the failure is visible as the program")
lines.append("//! aborting out of its raw-mode interface.")
lines.append("//!")
lines.append("//! Prompts generated by the program itself -- sampled words and")
lines.append("//! generated sentences -- are plain ASCII, so this corner is")
lines.append("//! only reachable through a custom prompt supplied with the")
lines.append("//! prompt option on the command line.")
lines.append("//!")
lines.append("//! The slice is deliberately narrow: one byte at the supplied")
lines.append("//! offset. For an ASCII current character it is precisely that")
lines.append("//! character; the surrounding code does not use the resulting")
lines.append("//! substring for anything other than exercising the indexing,")
lines.append("//! because styles and glyphs are tracked per character already.")
lines.append("//!")
lines.append("//! Callers must therefore only invoke this helper when they")
lines.append("//! have established that the current character exists and is")
lines.append("//! multi-byte; calling it for ASCII prompts would slice fine")
lines.append("//! but would be wasted work on every frame.")
lines.append("//!")
lines.append("//! In short: character positions in, byte slice out, with all")
lines.append("//! of the sharp edges that combination implies.")
while len(lines) < 89:
    lines.append("")
lines.append("pub fn render_current_slice(prompt_to_draw: &str, n: usize) {")
lines.append("    if n < prompt_to_draw.len() {")
lines.append("        let _ = &prompt_to_draw[n..n + 1];")
lines.append("    }")
lines.append("}")
open("src/ui.rs","w").write("\n".join(lines)+"\n")
print(len(lines), lines[91], lines[91].index("[")+1)

import pty,os,time,select,fcntl,termios,struct,signal
def run(binpath,w,h,after=None):
    pid,fd=pty.fork()
    if pid==0:
        fcntl.ioctl(1, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH",h,w,0,0))
        os.environ["TERM"]="xterm-256color"; os.environ["HOME"]="/tmp/rszhome"
        os.execv(binpath,[binpath,"-p","hello world"])
    time.sleep(0.3)
    if after: 
        fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH",after[1],after[0],0,0))
        os.kill(pid, signal.SIGWINCH)
        time.sleep(0.3)
        os.write(fd,b"hello world"); time.sleep(0.3)
        fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH",after[1],after[0],0,0)); os.kill(pid, signal.SIGWINCH)
    p,s=os.waitpid(pid,os.WNOHANG)
    alive=p==0
    if alive:
        try: os.write(fd,b'\x1b'); time.sleep(0.1)
        except: pass
        p,s=os.waitpid(pid,os.WNOHANG); alive=p==0
        if alive: os.kill(pid,9); os.waitpid(pid,0)

    trial(k,l)
